# A monument to something that never happened

A monument to something that never happened (Polish: Pomnik czegoś, co nigdy się nie wydarzyło (28.03.1983) ) – is a sculpture designed by Wilhelm Sasnal located in  Mościce.
Location
The sculpture is located in Mościce, a district in the western side of Tarnow. It has been installed in the green space on Chemiczna Street, near the tracks of railway line 91, close to Tarnów Mościce station and Jaskółcze Gniazdo Municipal Stadium.
Design
visible in the background along railway line 91.]]
The designer of the sculpture, Wilhelm Sasnal, is a Polish artist that comes from Mościce. He constructed his creation from 14 concrete sewer rings, arranged in the shape of a pyramid and coated with adhesive. The structure is about 4 metres high. A random date is inscribed in one of the circles: 28 • 3 •1983; According to the artist, this is the moment when a major disaster could have occurred: a threat that never materialised. The artwork was unveiled on 28 August 2010 as part of the Tarnów project 1000 lat nowoczesności (English: 1000 Years of Modernity).
Meaning
The monument is intended to evoke a sense of threat that was ever-present in Mościce’s social landscape prior to 1989, and thus during the Cold War, prior to the fall of the Iron Curtain and the political transformation in Poland. Sasnal claimed that this fear stemmed from the potential danger posed to the town by the nearby large chemical plant – the Nitrogen Works in Tarnów-Mościce. In addition to chemical hazards, residents were also terrified by rumours of American long-range missiles targeting the factory – a strategic facility. According to the artist’s intention, the monument is intended to present an alternative vision of the past, in which an unspecified but tragically devastating apocalypse has occurred.
The location was deliberately chosen for its seclusion, as, according to the artist’s vision, the monument is meant to be hidden, eventually overgrown with grass and other vegetation, and ultimately forgotten.
Controversy
The sculpture, in keeping with its original intention, looks temporary. As a result, some residents view it merely as material left behind for the construction of the pipeline, and not  a work of art. The development was controversial because of its location: it was ideally situated for the failed expansion of the car park at the nearby football and speedway stadium.
Legacy
The monument has attracted attention within academic and artistic circles. References to the work have appeared in academic publications as well as in specialist media covering Polish culture and architecture.
